name: Mount Kumotori from Kamosawa (雲取山)
why: Tokyo's highest summit, 2,017 m, reached on a long, even forest path and an open ridge with Mount Fuji to the south, with a night in a big hut just below the top.
book: No permit; file a climbing plan (tozan todoke). Nishi Tokyo bus from Okutama station to Kamosawa, about 35 minutes; buses are few on weekdays. Book the night at Kumotori Sanso, 20 minutes below the summit, or at Nanatsuishi-goya (reservations generally needed, self-catering). Okutama-goya on the ridge is closed.
water: Carry 2 litres from Kamosawa. Drinks are sold at Nanatsuishi-goya and Kumotori Sanso; there is a spring by the Sanso.
dangers: A long day: about 5.5 hours and 1,450 m up to the summit. Start the climb by 09:00.
Loose small stones on the steep ridge sections: slippery coming down on day 2.
In October and November it gets dark around 16:00: carry a headlamp.
Snow and ice on the ridge from December: then it is a winter climb.
turnaround: Not at Mount Nanatsuishi (about 4 hours up) by 14:00: sleep at Nanatsuishi-goya if you booked, or go back down.

points.name: Kamosawa bus stop
points.note: Above Lake Okutama, about 530 m. Walk 30 minutes up the road through cedar forest to the car park and the trail entrance.

points.name: Nanatsuishi-goya
points.note: The small hut at about 1,600 m, after the steep bamboo-grass slope. From Mount Nanatsuishi above, the wide open ridge leads north-west to Kumotori.

points.name: Kumotori summit
points.note: 2,017 m, the highest point of Tokyo, with an emergency shelter. On a clear morning Mount Fuji stands to the south-west.

points.name: Kumotori Sanso
points.note: The large two-storey hut 20 minutes down the north side of the summit. Day 2: climb back over the top for sunrise and walk down the same way to Kamosawa.
